examples.en: The moon is hidden behind the clouds, so I can't see it.

examples.ko: 앞사람 키가 커서 화면이 반쯤 가려졌어요.
examples.en: The person in front is tall, so half the screen is blocked.

examples.ko: 나무에 가려져서 간판이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The sign is hidden by the trees and is hard to see.

examples.ko: 가방을 이불로 덮었지만 다 가려지지 않았어요.
examples.en: I covered the bag with a blanket, but it wasn't completely hidden.

examples.ko: 이 커튼을 치면 창문이 완전히 가려질까요?
examples.en: If I close this curtain, will the window be fully covered?

examples.ko: 큰 건물에 가려져서 바다가 안 보여요.
examples.en: The sea is hidden by the big building, so I can't see it.

explain: '가리다'의 피동으로, 무엇이 앞을 막아서 안 보이게 되었다는 느낌이에요. 단순히 '안 보이다'보다 막고 있는 것이 있다는 점이 달라요. '승부가 가려지다'처럼 결과가 분명하게 정해질 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 모자에 가려진 얼굴이 잘 안 보여요.
phrases.en: I can't see the face hidden by the hat well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가려지다'를 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 말(-ㄴ)로 바꿔서, 무엇에 막혀 안 보이는 대상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of the verb, used to describe a thing that is blocked from view.

phrases.en: The sun was hidden by the clouds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 가려진 상황을 해요체 과거형으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense in polite speech, used to say that something has already become blocked from view.

phrases.example: 커튼을 쳐도 창문이 다 가려지지 않아요.
phrases.en: Even with the curtain closed, the window isn't fully covered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 완전히 막히지 않고 조금 보일 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form, used when something is not fully blocked and can still be seen.

explain_en: It is the passive of '가리다', and it feels like something is standing in front and blocking the view. Compared with plain '안 보이다', it points to something that is blocking. It is also used when a result gets clearly decided, as in '승부가 가려지다'.

en: to be paid; to be settled

examples.en: Please check whether it can be paid by card.
The ordered item is paid for automatically.

examples.ko: 실수로 같은 물건이 두 번 결제됐어요.
examples.en: The same item was charged twice by mistake.
A text arrives once it is paid, so please check.

examples.ko: 아직 결제되지 않아서 상품을 보낼 수 없어요.
examples.en: It hasn't been paid yet, so we can't send the goods.

examples.ko: 결제된 금액은 다음 달에 카드값에서 빠져요.
examples.en: The amount that was paid comes out of the card bill next month.

explain: '결제하다'는 사람이 돈을 내는 일이고, '결제되다'는 결제가 처리된 상태를 말해요. 앱, 인터넷 쇼핑, 카드 문자에서 자주 나와요. 가게에서 직접 낼 때는 '계산하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The card payment doesn't go through in the app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결제가 처리되지 않을 때 쓰는 말이에요. 앱이나 인터넷 쇼핑 문제를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when a payment does not get processed. It is common for app and online shopping problems.

phrases.en: Check your text message to see if the order payment went through.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는지'는 결과를 모를 때 확인하는 말이에요. 카드 문자와 같이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-neunji' is used when you check an unknown result. It often goes with card text messages.

phrases.en: It was charged twice by mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 돈이 두 번 나갔다는 문제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to report a problem where the same payment was charged twice.

explain_en: 결제하다 is a person paying, while 결제되다 states that the payment has been processed. It shows up in apps, online shopping and card text messages. At a shop counter, 계산하다 sounds more natural.

dis.h: payment processed, esp. by card or transaction

p.n: 결제 stresses the transaction going through; 지불 just says the money was paid.

examples.en: The road curves to the right.
The wire bent easily.
If your back is bent, it can hurt.
It's an old nail, so it bends easily.

examples.ko: 구부러진 길을 따라 걸으면 바다가 나와요.
examples.en: If you walk along the curved road, you reach the sea.
As she grew older, my grandmother's back became bent.

explain: 물건이나 길이 저절로 휘어 있는 상태를 말해요. 사람이 일부러 구부릴 때는 '구부리다'를 써서 '무릎을 구부리다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: Please walk along the curved road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 모양을 설명하는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used before a noun to describe its shape.

phrases.en: This stick doesn't bend easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단단해서 휘지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is stiff and does not bend.

phrases.en: The branch bent in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이고, 힘을 받아 둥글게 되는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, with a stronger sense of curving under force.

explain_en: It describes a thing or road that is bent on its own. When a person bends something on purpose, use '구부리다', as in '무릎을 구부리다' (bend one's knees).

examples.en: The tree roots stretch deep into the ground.
A tree root was sticking out of the road and I almost tripped.
Many trees were pulled out by the roots in the typhoon.
Please give plenty of water around the tree's roots.

examples.ko: 이 나무뿌리는 말려서 차로 끓여 마셔요.
examples.en: You dry this tree root and boil it as tea.
The paving stones are lifted up because of the tree roots.

explain: 그냥 '뿌리'라고 해도 돼요. 나무인 것을 분명히 하고 싶을 때 '나무뿌리'라고 말해요. '뿌리'는 '문제의 뿌리'처럼 근본을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: This plant has long roots.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나무뿌리'보다 짧고 식물 전체에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter than 나무뿌리 and works for any plant.

phrases.en: I tripped on a tree root on the mountain path.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에 튀어나온 뿌리에 발이 걸릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when your foot catches on a root sticking out.
phrases.en_equiv: to trip on a tree root

phrases.example: 이 나무는 나무뿌리가 깊어서 잘 쓰러지지 않아요.
phrases.en: This tree has deep roots, so it doesn't fall over easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뿌리의 길이를 말할 때 형용사와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with an adjective to describe how deep roots are.

explain_en: You can simply say '뿌리'. People say '나무뿌리' when they want to make clear it is a tree's root. '뿌리' is also used figuratively for the origin of something, as in '문제의 뿌리'.

examples.en: I watched a baseball game in a dome.

examples.ko: 돔 안에서는 비가 와도 경기를 해요.
examples.en: Inside the dome, games go on even when it rains.
This city's dome is also used as a concert hall.

examples.ko: 돔의 지붕이 열리는 모습을 처음 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the dome's roof open for the first time.
In autumn, I go to the dome to see concerts.
When the dome is closed, sound echoes loudly.

explain: 영어 dome에서 온 외래어예요. 한국에서는 '고척스카이돔'처럼 지붕이 있는 경기장 이름에 나와요. 지붕이 있는 야구장을 '돔구장'이라고도 불러요.

phrases.en: I go to the dome stadium on weekends to watch baseball.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지붕이 있는 야구장을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a baseball stadium with a roof.

phrases.en: It's cool inside the dome even in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '안'을 붙여 지붕 아래 안쪽 공간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '안' refers to the space inside the dome.

phrases.en: This concert is held at the dome.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에서'를 붙여 경기나 행사가 돔에서 한다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '에서', it says a game or event takes place at the dome.
phrases.en_equiv: to be held at the dome

explain_en: It is a loanword from the English 'dome'. In Korea it appears in the names of roofed stadiums such as '고척스카이돔'. A baseball park with a roof is also called '돔구장'.

examples.ko: 이렇게 큰 상을 받다니 아직도 믿어지지 않아요.
examples.en: I still can't believe I won such a big prize.
Can you believe that you're graduating already?

examples.ko: 그 이야기는 너무 이상해서 쉽게 믿어지지 않았어요.
examples.en: That story was so strange that it was hard to believe.
Now that I've seen the photo myself, I can finally believe it.

examples.ko: 그 믿어지지 않는 일이 요즘 눈앞에서 벌어지고 있어요.
examples.en: That unbelievable thing is happening right before my eyes these days.

examples.ko: 저 사람이 한 말은 이상하게 믿어지는 힘이 있어요.
examples.en: What that person says has a strange power that makes you believe it.

explain: '믿다'와 달리 내 의지와 상관없이 마음에서 그렇게 느껴진다는 느낌이에요. 놀랍거나 실감이 안 날 때 '믿어지지 않아요'라고 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '믿기지 않아요'도 써요.

phrases.en: I can't believe I passed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '믿어지지 않다'와 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '믿어지지 않다', and more common in speech.

phrases.en: Something unbelievable happened.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라운 일이나 소식을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a surprising event or news.

phrases.en: I just can't believe that story.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도저히'를 붙이면 전혀 믿을 수 없다는 느낌이 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '도저히' strengthens the feeling that it's impossible to believe.

explain_en: Unlike '믿다', it feels as if the belief happens in your heart regardless of your will. You say '믿어지지 않아요' when something is surprising or hard to take in. '믿기지 않아요' is used with the same meaning.

en: to come off; to be taken off

examples.ko: 길을 가다가 갑자기 구두가 벗겨지는 바람에 민망했어요.
examples.en: My shoe suddenly came off while I was walking, and I felt embarrassed.
My socks keep slipping off, and it bothers me.
The paint on the door has peeled off from long use.
My sunburned skin is peeling in white flakes.
My shoes are big, so they keep coming off when I run.

examples.ko: 이 감자 껍질은 쉽게 벗겨지지 않아요.
examples.en: The skin of this potato doesn't come off easily.

explain: '벗다'는 사람이 일부러 옷이나 신발을 벗는 것이지만, '벗겨지다'는 신발·껍질·페인트·피부가 저절로 떨어질 때 써요. 누가 일부러 벗길 때는 '벗기다'라고 해요. 머리에 쓰면 '머리가 벗겨지다'처럼 대머리가 된다는 뜻이 돼요.

phrases.example: 아버지는 나이가 들면서 머리가 벗겨지기 시작했어요.
phrases.en: As my father got older, he started to go bald.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리카락이 빠져서 두피가 드러난다는 뜻이에요. 조금 직접적인 표현이라 사람 앞에서는 조심해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means hair falls out and the scalp shows. It is a rather direct expression, so be careful using it in front of people.

explain_en: '벗다' is when a person takes off clothes or shoes on purpose, while '벗겨지다' is for shoes, peels, paint or skin that come off by themselves. When someone takes it off deliberately, you use '벗기다'. Said about hair, as in '머리가 벗겨지다', it means going bald.

en: to be performed; to be played

examples.en: A piano piece is played in the concert hall.
That song was played on the guitar.

examples.ko: 이 곡은 결혼식에서 자주 연주되곤 해요.
examples.en: This piece is often played at weddings.
The music being played is really gentle.

examples.ko: 오늘 밤 새 곡이 처음 연주될 거예요.
examples.en: A new piece will be performed for the first time tonight.
The piece couldn't be played because there was no instrument.

explain: '연주되다'는 악기로 음악이 들릴 때 써요. 노래를 부르는 일에는 안 써요. '곡이 연주되다'처럼 곡이 주어예요. 사람이 하면 '피아노를 연주하다'예요.

phrases.en: Music is being played on the stage now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 진행 중인 연주를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a performance happening right now.

phrases.en: That piece is played at the concert.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디에서 연주되는지 장소를 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when naming the place where it is played.

phrases.en: I play the guitar every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 말이에요. '연주되다'는 곡이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person is the subject; '연주되다' takes the piece as subject.

explain_en: 연주되다 is used when music is heard from instruments. It isn't used for singing. The piece is the subject, as in '곡이 연주되다'. When a person does it, use '피아노를 연주하다'.

p.n: 공연되다 refers to a whole show, not a piece being played.

examples.en: The main gate was closed, so I went in through the side door.

examples.ko: 이 건물 옆문은 밤에 잠겨 있어요.
examples.en: This building's side door is locked at night.
I'll wait in front of the building's side door.
Excuse me, do you know where the side door is?
Please leave the package at the side door of the house.

examples.ko: 옆문을 열어 두면 바람이 잘 통해요.
examples.en: If you leave the side door open, the air flows well.

explain: '정문', '후문', '뒷문'처럼 문의 위치로 구분해서 부르는 말이에요. 건물이나 집의 옆쪽에 있는 작은 출입구를 가리킬 때 써요. 발음은 [염문]이에요.

phrases.en: The main gate was far, so I went in through the side door.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'와 함께 어느 문으로 가는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '으로' to say which door you use.
phrases.en_equiv: to go in by the side door

phrases.en: The side door is open, so come that way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문의 상태를 알려 주며 길을 안내할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone the door's state while giving directions.

phrases.en: Let's meet in front of the side door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속 장소를 정할 때 쓰는 짧은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short phrase for setting a meeting spot.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the side door

explain_en: Like '정문' (main gate), '후문' (rear gate) and '뒷문' (back door), it names a door by its position. It points to a smaller entrance on the side of a building or house. It is pronounced [염문].

en: to be managed; to be operated; to be run

examples.en: This school is run with government support.
Until last year this library operated only on weekdays.

examples.ko: 이 카페는 아침 일곱 시부터 운영되고 있어요.
examples.en: This cafe is open for business from seven in the morning.

examples.ko: 잘 운영되는 가게는 손님이 계속 와요.
examples.en: A well-run shop keeps getting customers.

examples.ko: 이 모임은 회비로 운영돼서 따로 돈을 내요.
examples.en: This group is run on membership fees, so we pay separately.

examples.ko: 규칙이 없으면 회사가 제대로 운영될 수 없어요.
examples.en: Without rules, a company can't be run properly.

explain: '운영하다'는 가게·회사·학교·서비스를 꾸려 가는 사람 쪽이고, '운영되다'는 그렇게 굴러가는 상태예요. 도서관·학교·공공시설은 '운영 시간', 가게는 '영업 시간'을 더 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 도서관 운영 시간은 오전 아홉 시부터예요.
phrases.en: The library's operating hours start at nine in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도서관, 학교 같은 공공시설이 문을 여는 시간을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the opening hours of public places like libraries and schools.

phrases.en: This center is run by the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 있다'를 붙여 지금 운영되는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-고 있다' means it is currently being run.

phrases.example: 이 가게는 잘 운영돼서 손님이 많아요.
phrases.en: This shop is run well, so it has lots of customers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잘'과 함께 문제없이 굴러간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '잘', it means it runs smoothly.

explain_en: '운영하다' is the person running a shop, company, school or service; '운영되다' is the state of it running. For libraries, schools and public facilities, '운영 시간' is common, while shops more often say '영업 시간'.

dis.h: run or operated as an ongoing service

p.n: 관리 means looked after or maintained, not necessarily run as a service.

en: to be used; to be utilized

examples.en: This building is used as a student lounge.
This transit card is used nationwide.
The leftover ingredients were used in another dish too.

examples.ko: 이 기술은 병원에서도 이용될 수 있어요.
examples.en: This technology can be used in hospitals too.
The longer it is used, the more the fee goes up.

examples.ko: 휴일에는 이 주차장이 무료로 이용되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I wish this parking lot could be used for free on holidays.

explain: '이용'은 시설·서비스·교통·자원을 활용하는 느낌이고, '사용'은 펜·단어·돈처럼 물건을 쓰는 느낌이에요. 도서관·지하철은 '이용', 펜·단어는 '사용'이 어울려요. 사람을 자기 이익으로 쓰면 '이용당하다'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: This word is used a lot in daily life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷한데, 물건이나 말을 쓸 때는 '사용되다'가 더 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, but better for things and words.

phrases.example: 이 광장은 시민 공원으로 이용되고 있어요.
phrases.en: This plaza is being used as a public park.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 있다'를 붙여 지금 그렇게 쓰이는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-고 있다' means it is currently being used that way.

phrases.en: This app is widely used across the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '널리'와 함께 많은 사람이나 곳에서 쓰인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '널리', it means used by many people or in many places.

explain_en: '이용' has the feel of making use of facilities, services, transport or resources, while '사용' is using objects like a pen, a word or money. A library or subway is '이용'; a pen or a word is '사용'. When a person is used for someone's gain, it becomes '이용당하다'.

dis.h: used as a means; may imply exploitation

p.n: 사용되다 is neutral. 이용되다 stresses being taken advantage of as a means.

examples.en: Old paintings are on display at the museum.
My work was displayed in the lobby.

examples.ko: 전시되는 옷은 만져 볼 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't touch the clothes on display.
The photos will be on display until next month.
The ring displayed in the glass case is pretty.
Do you want to go see the paintings when they are displayed?

explain: 보여 주려고 놓인 물건이 주어일 때 써요. 사람이나 기관이 보여 주면 '전시하다'예요. 가게나 박물관 이야기에 나와요.

phrases.en: The students' paintings are on display in the lobby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 놓여서 지금 볼 수 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of already being set out so people can see it now.

phrases.en: The new work is on display right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 전시하는 기간이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the exhibition period is now.

explain_en: Use it when the object put out for viewing is the subject. If a person or institution shows it, use '전시하다'. It appears in talk about shops and museums.

examples.en: This restaurant is often recommended in reviews.
Minsu was nominated as the representative.
It's a book recommended for beginners.

examples.ko: 이 방법은 더 이상 추천되지 않아요.
examples.en: This method is no longer recommended.
You will be put forward as a good candidate.
I took a cold medicine that many people recommend.

explain: 물건이나 방법이 주어이면 '사람들에게 권해진다'는 뜻이고, 사람이 주어이면 '후보로 올려진다'는 뜻이에요. 내가 권할 때는 '추천하다'를 써요. 추천받는 사람은 '에게', 추천한 쪽은 '에 의해'로 나타내요.

phrases.en: I watched the recommended movie at the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 권한 것을 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for something people have recommended.

phrases.en: Sumi was recommended as a candidate for class president.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 주어일 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when the subject is a person.

phrases.en: I got a recommendation for this restaurant from a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추천을 받은 사람이 주어이고, 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The subject is the person who got the recommendation, and it's more common in speech.

explain_en: With an item or method as the subject, it means people recommend it. With a person as the subject, it means being put forward as a candidate. When you are the one recommending, use '추천하다'. The person it is recommended to takes 에게, and the recommender takes 에 의해.

examples.en: A shirt collar is hard to iron.

examples.ko: 칼라 있는 옷을 입고 면접에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the interview in clothes with a collar.
You look cool when you stand up the collar.
This coat has a big collar.
The collar got dirty, so I washed it.
I buttoned it all the way up to the collar.

explain: '컬러'(색)와 소리가 비슷해서 헷갈려요. 옷의 목 부분은 '칼라', 색은 '컬러'라고 써요.

phrases.en: This T-shirt has no collar, so it's comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷에 목 부분 칼라가 없을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a piece of clothing has no collar.

phrases.en: I wear a collared shirt to work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '칼라'를 앞에 붙여 칼라가 있는 셔츠를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting 'collar' in front names a shirt that has a collar.

phrases.en: The wind was blowing, so I turned up my collar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추울 때 칼라를 위로 올리는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes lifting the collar up when it is cold.

explain_en: It sounds close to 'keolleo' (color), which causes mix-ups. The neck part of clothing is 'kalla'; color is 'keolleo'.

en: to be dug out; to become hollowed or dented

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 길바닥이 크게 파이고 물이 고였어요.
examples.en: After heavy rain, the road got a big hole and water collected.

examples.ko: 도로에 파인 곳이 많아서 조심해서 걸어요.
examples.en: There are many holes in the road, so I walk carefully.

examples.ko: 파도에 바닷가 모래가 파이는 모습을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the beach sand being scooped out by the waves.

examples.ko: 바퀴 자국이 깊게 파이면 차가 지나가기 힘들어요.
examples.en: If the tire tracks get deep, it's hard for cars to pass.

examples.ko: 한 곳에 물이 계속 떨어지면 바위도 파이게 돼요.
examples.en: If water keeps dripping in one spot, even rock gets worn into a hollow.

examples.ko: 삽으로 땅을 팠는데 생각보다 잘 파이지 않아요.
examples.en: I dug the ground with a shovel, but it doesn't dig out as easily as I thought.

explain: '파다'는 사람이 구덩이를 만드는 일이고, '파이다'는 비, 바퀴, 물 때문에 저절로 구덩이가 생긴 모습이에요. '파여요', '파였어요'처럼 줄여서 써요.

phrases.example: 비가 와서 마당 한가운데가 움푹 파였어요.
phrases.en: Because of the rain, the middle of the yard was dug out in a deep dent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅이 깊게 들어간 모양을 더 분명하게 말할 때 '움푹'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 움푹 describes the deep, sunken shape more clearly.

phrases.en: Rainwater collected in the dented spot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구덩이가 생긴 자리를 가리킬 때 '파이다'를 '파인'으로 바꿔 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Changes to 파인 to point at the spot where a dent has formed.

phrases.example: 바닥이 단단해서 비가 와도 파이지 않아요.
phrases.en: The ground is hard, so it does not get dug out even when it rains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구덩이가 생기지 않는다고 부정으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, saying no dent forms.

explain_en: '파다' is when a person digs a hole, while '파이다' is when rain, wheels, or water cause a hole to form by itself. It contracts to forms like '파여요' and '파였어요'.
